title.narrative: Reducing Impact of Acute Malnutrition amongst under 5 children and Improving Nutrition practices amongst Caregivers in Marte and Magumeri (Re.I.A.Ch.I.N.)

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to mitigate and address the impact of the lean season in Marte and Magumeri LGA, Northeast of Nigeria. The crisis has been aggravated by several factors, including frequent displacements, food insecurity, climate change, biting inflation, as well as government policies such as camp closure, and government decisions on certain humanitarian interventions. This project aims to reduce the impact of the lean season crisis by providing nutritional care (Curative intervention) for children under 5 with acute malnutrition and improving the knowledge of caregivers (Preventive intervention) to better support their families.ltbrgtThis intervention will be carried out in both Magumeri and Marte, targeting 20,929 children under 5 and their caregivers. 5TEi will offer preventive and curative services, reaching 34,404 people with nutrition-sensitive and specific interventions. The project will carry out prepositioning of nutrition supplies. Additionally, it will mainstream disability inclusion and PSEA/GBV prevention into its programming. ltbrgtIn Marte, preventive intervention will include family MUAC, IYCF counselling using MTMSG and FtFSGs established in the community. The distribution of MNP and SQ-LNS will also be carried out by CNMs. For curative interventions, an OTP will be set up in MCH Marte to support the treatment of SAM without complications. The caregivers of the children will also receive MIYCN counselling in the OTP in addition to GBV/PSEA prevention measures.ltbrgtIn Magumeri, 5TEi activities will include the set-up of OTP in the Gajiganna and Magumeri outscage area to manage cases of SAM without complication and community nutrition activities. The latter activities are preventive and include the use of MtMSg and FtFSG to deliver MIYCN messaging aimed at improving IYCF practices amongst caregivers. Family MUAC activities will also be extended to hard-to-reach locations within Magumeri.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt5TEi has an active presence in both Marte and Magumeri LGAs, where we have built strong community trust and functional networks through ongoing community-based HIV programs. These existing structures enable us to effectively mobilize, implement, and monitor interventions, especially in hard-to-reach areas. Our deep familiarity with the terrain, strong engagement with local stakeholders, and established operational footprint make us well-positioned to deliver timely and efficient nutrition services where few actors are present. This new effort will build on 5TEi’s ongoing work in these LGAs, particularly to fill the gaps left by recent cuts in USAID funding, leveraging our existing infrastructure to strengthen nutrition interventions and reach the most vulnerable.ltbrgtlt/pgt
